why_this_file_exists: block_record_round1.json and live_feasibility_round1.json are pinned evidence on the W14-01 row, and both point the unlock at W12-02 as the card that would supply a runtime worker. That attribution is wrong. W14-01 is still blocked, but for a larger reason that no card owns, and leaving the earlier wording alone would send the next window to the wrong card.

what_was_measured.the_client_side_exists: internal/domain/runtime_broker_windows.go:31 declares Endpoint on the provider record, :78 parses it, and :183-194 POSTs the envelope {key, epoch, run_id, capability, payload} with Content-Type application/json, an Idempotency-Key and a bearer token, with Proxy: nil, DisableKeepAlives and a CheckRedirect that refuses every redirect.
what_was_measured.no_server_side_in_product_code: git grep -l ListenAndServe over tracked files returns only ops/remote_access/gateway/main.go (an unrelated remote-access gateway) plus two files under execution/verifier (a snapshot copy and a review note). Nothing in internal/, apps/ or adapters/ opens a listener that could receive the broker's POST.
what_was_measured.what_adapters_runtime_actually_is: adapters/runtime carries worker ADMISSION and isolation, not a worker endpoint: bridge_windows.go validates dispatch_key, epoch >= 1, the sandbox profile appcontainer-zero-capabilities-v1 and adapter_revision, tracks a journal, lease and wall deadline, and runtime_windows.go builds the CODEX_HOME environment. grep for exec.Command / StdinPipe inside adapters/runtime returns nothing, so it does not spawn a coding-agent process either.
what_was_measured.the_plan_has_one_owner_of_that_path_and_: Scanning all 71 steps of contracts/execution.plan.json for write_scope containing adapters/runtime returns exactly one card, W12-02 用途等价资源切换与用户可操作请求, whose actions are failover between purpose-equivalent resources, aggregated ResourceRequest, proving unaffected branches continue, and the U09 value-checkpoint rule. Building the envelope server is not among them.

consequence: The LIVE half of this line - W14-01, its formal cases A13/A04/C23, and any parent gate that requires a real model cycle - depends on a component the 71-card plan never assigns to anyone. That is a plan gap, not merely a missing resource: blocking W14-01 on 'W12-02 will deliver a worker' would be a false promise to the next window, and quietly writing that worker under another card's write scope would be out of scope on this line.
what_i_did_not_do: I did not implement an envelope server under adapters/runtime (that is W12-02's path for different work), did not spend the authorized provider call against a path that has no listener to answer it, and did not edit the two pinned records that carry the earlier, wrong attribution.
decision_needed: Either a card's scope is extended by its owner to include the worker endpoint, or the LIVE cards stay blocked and the objective is reported with that gap named. The cheapest honest next step is to ask, rather than to invent a scope. Until then W14-01 stays BLOCKED with this file as the reason, and the checkpoint obligation records the unowned component so it is not lost.
corrections: block_record_round1.json and live_feasibility_round1.json each say the owner of the missing worker is W12-02 (adapters/runtime). Measured above: W12-02 owns the path but not that work, and no step in execution.plan.json builds the envelope server.
